title: Take-up Rate of Caregiving Respite Services
what_it_is: Take-up Rate of Caregiving Respite Services

sections.label: Respite care demand and enhancements
sections.summary: Providers generally meet respite care demand, with over 14,600 seniors' and 3,600 PwDs' caregivers using subsidised services in 2025, and planned enhancements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Providers are generally able to meet the demand for respite care, with the Agency for Integrated Care and SG Enable working with providers to prioritise clients with urgent care needs, including cases with caregivers seeking help to cope with burnout.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In 2025, caregivers of over 14,600 seniors and over 3,600 PwDs and children with developmental needs utilised subsidised respite care services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: For instance, we will enhance the Home Personal Care service later this year to offer longer service hours and after-hours care, including for respite care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Take-a-Break home-based respite programme for PwDs and children with developmental needs is also currently being reviewed.
